issues.legal_issue: A public servant is protected from criminal cognizance without prior governmental sanction when the acts alleged have a reasonable connection with the discharge or purported discharge of official duties.
material_facts: The accused was a Sub-Divisional Officer and was present in his official capacity to supervise a drive to remove encroachments from government roadside land.

During the operation, the complainant alleged that the accused and accompanying officials entered the complainant’s clinic, used abusive language, directed that the complainant be removed, and carried out demolitions.
The alleged conduct occurred in the course of the encroachment-removal operation, which the accused was supervising as part of his official duties.
No prior sanction for prosecution had been obtained.
issues.conclusion: The allegations had a reasonable nexus with the accused’s official duty, so cognizance could not be taken without prior sanction. The High Court’s order was set aside and the cognizance order was quashed, without preventing the competent authority from obtaining sanction and proceeding in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure bars a court from taking cognizance without prior governmental sanction where the accused is a public servant removable only by or with governmental sanction and the alleged offence was committed while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of official duty. The alleged act must have a reasonable connection with the duty; it need not be strictly necessary to perform that duty, and an act that exceeds what the duty requires may still be protected if it is sufficiently interrelated with the duty. The protection does not place an official above the law for acts unconnected with official duty. Section 197 is an exception to the general cognizance power under Section 190. The court may consider whether sanction is required at any stage, and the question concerns the court’s jurisdiction. The court relied on Matajog Dobey v. H.C. Bhari, Suresh Kumar Bhikamchand Jain v. Pandey Ajay Bhushan, State through the CBI v. B.L. Verma, and N.K. Ogle v. Sanwaldas Alias Sanwalmal Ahuja.

rule.if: criminal_cognizance_proceeding and protected_public_servant and acts_during_official_task and not prior_sanction

predicates.criminal_cognizance_proceeding: A criminal proceeding seeks a court’s cognizance of alleged offences by a public servant.
predicates.protected_public_servant: The accused is a public servant who can be removed from office only by or with governmental sanction.
predicates.acts_during_official_task: The conduct complained of occurred while the public servant was carrying out or purporting to carry out an assigned official task.
predicates.prior_sanction: The competent government authority granted sanction for prosecution before the court took cognizance.
predicates.cognizance_cannot_be_taken_without_prior: A court cannot take cognizance of the alleged offence unless prior governmental sanction has been obtained.

issues.definition: When a criminal cognizance proceeding concerns a protected public servant, the alleged conduct occurred during an official task, and prior sanction is absent, cognizance cannot be taken without prior sanction.
